![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14130082/assets/82439d51448a442dede4b3965ecbbd2f2daa7b2365ea75c80951478fd10af65c.png)

Use the model above to calculate $\dfrac{4}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{3}.$
question.worked_solution:
Since we need to multiply by $\dfrac{1}{\color{blue}3}$, we split the whole into $\color{blue}3$ equal parts horizontally.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14130082/assets/a95b378064e6ec2ed15637fd05ea49e5f988bfb30d8ae788a7b2086ff920a65f.png)

From the picture on the right, we obtain that the shaded part represents $\dfrac{4}{15}$ of the whole.

Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{4}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{4}{15}.
$$
